## Context / Problem

This story re-lands the scanner integration artifacts that were reverted after Gerrit change 2612. The prior landing wired `scanner-integration` directly into the required `Verified` vote aggregate in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`; when that lane failed on full-route changes, incident `90c7-c465-4037-42d5` showed the result was a self-referential lock that prevented the repair/revert from earning `Verified +1`.

ADR 0114 (`docs/adr/0114-advisory-gate-before-hot-path.md`) now requires any new check that may eventually enter the required `Verified` hot path to run advisory first: non-voting, non-blocking, and outside the aggregate's required `needs`, routing conditions, and any other vote-casting wiring. Promotion into the voting path is explicitly out of scope for this ticket and requires a separate future change after the advisory lane has demonstrated a passing run on `main`.

## Scope

Recreate the reverted scanner artifacts from change 2612 as a starting point, adapting them to current `origin/main` and the post-revert parity guards:

- platform-aware scanner manifest at `infra/compose/review-scanners.lock.json` plus per-platform Semgrep hash locks for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`;
- scanner provisioning helper and review-bot Dockerfile integration, including the current-main relative-prefix regression fix (the Semgrep link must remain executable when the Makefile passes a relative `.tools/review-scanners` prefix from another working directory);
- a POSIX-`dash`-safe Make target for explicit scanner integration validation;
- unit/contract tests for manifest selection, checksum/hash rejection, scanner contract execution, workflow wiring, documentation generation, and public exposure;
- reusable scanner workflow plus mirror-CI wiring and a separate Gerrit exact-patchset advisory workflow outside `gerrit-verify.yaml`;
- generated `docs/security.md` scanner-lock ownership, update, checksum, and recovery narrative.

## Advisory wiring constraint

The recreated Gerrit scanner lane must be advisory only and must live outside `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` as a separate workflow dispatch. It must not be listed in the `vote` job's `needs`, must not appear in the vote normalization expression, must not be present in the same workflow run observed by `im-open/workflow-conclusion`, and must not otherwise affect the required `Verified` aggregate. The `vote` job must remain able to cast `Verified +1/-1` from the existing required lanes even if the advisory scanner lane fails. Do not promote scanner integration into the voting path in this change.

## Testing

Use RED-first held-out TDD for the behavioral/static contract that proves the advisory job is outside `vote.needs` while still present for full-route Gerrit runs. Recreate and adapt the reverted tests for the scanner manifest, installer, generated docs, workflow exposure, and native scanner contracts. Preserve b973 parity: `_scanner-integration.yml` and any local-uses path that reaches it must carry the predates-gate `[ -f … ]` guard, and the Make recipe must avoid bash-only constructs (`set -o pipefail`, `[[ … ]]`, arrays, here-strings, and `${var^}`/`${var,}`).

Before final gates, rebase onto latest `origin/main`, regenerate docs, and verify `docs/config-reference.md` does not drift unexpectedly from the scanner documentation generator change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The reverted scanner artifacts are recreated and adapted against current `origin/main` without editing outside the recorded 18-path file impact.
- [ ] `infra/compose/review-scanners.lock.json` has independent `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` scanner entries, each with an exact Gitleaks URL and SHA-256 sourced from the matching release checksums asset.
- [ ] Each platform entry points to a fully resolved Semgrep requirements lock with the same top-level Semgrep version and all required distribution hashes; the installer uses `pip install --require-hashes`.
- [ ] The review-bot Docker build selects and validates the `linux/arm64` entry, while the reusable Linux x64 CI lane selects and validates the `linux/amd64` entry.
- [ ] The installer rejects an unsupported platform, a missing scanner, the wrong Gitleaks version/digest, and invalid Semgrep requirement hashes before running the focused contracts.
- [ ] Valid selected scanner locks allow the explicit native-binary target to run the real Semgrep/Gitleaks integration contracts, while default local tests and unsupported local platforms preserve skip-with-reason behavior and do not provision scanners.
- [ ] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` owns a curated scanner-lock security narrative; regenerated `docs/security.md` names the manifest as the update authority, the checksum source, a concrete per-platform bump example, and the withdrawn-asset recovery procedure.
- [ ] The scanner workflow includes the b973 predates-gate guard and the scanner Make recipe is POSIX-`dash`-safe under `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` and `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`.
- [ ] The scanner lane is wired as advisory for Gerrit: it is non-voting, non-blocking, outside `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` `vote.needs`, and not used by the required `Verified` aggregate or route decision.
- [ ] Mirror CI may run the reusable scanner lane for visibility, but Gerrit `Verified` voting remains governed only by the existing required aggregate.
- [ ] OpenGrep, Docker-image builds, normal `make lint`, and default local tests remain outside scope.
- [ ] The lane's expected cold-run cost is documented as approximately 1.5-3 runner-minutes without extending the existing 22-23 minute critical path when capacity is available.
